title: Wetlands Conservation and Access Improvement Act of 2025
official_summary:
Wetlands Conservation and Access Improvement Act of 2025

This act extends until FY2033 a requirement for the interest earned on certain funds held in the Federal Aid to Wildlife Restoration Fund to be distributed to states for carrying out certain wildlife conservation and restoration programs. Specifically, the act extends the period in which the interest earned on revenue generated from excise taxes on certain firearms, ammunition, and archery equipment must be used for wildlife conservation and restoration programs established under the North American Wetlands Conservation Act. This requirement was set to expire at the beginning of FY2026. In the absence of this requirement, this funding would be distributed to states, according to a formula, for (1) wildlife restoration, (2) hunter education and safety, (3) multistate conservation grants, and (4) administrative costs.

summary.headline: Law keeps sending interest from a federal wildlife fund to wetlands conservation programs through fiscal year 2033.
summary.what_it_does: Excise taxes on certain guns, ammunition, and archery gear go into a federal wildlife fund, and that money earns interest. A rule required the interest to pay for wetlands conservation programs under the North American Wetlands Conservation Act, but that rule was set to end when fiscal year 2026 began. This law extends the rule through fiscal year 2033. Without it, the interest would have been shared with states by formula for wildlife restoration, hunter education and safety, multistate conservation grants, and administrative costs.

who_it_affects.group: Groups that receive North American Wetlands Conservation Act funding
who_it_affects.how: They keep getting the interest from the wildlife fund for wetlands conservation and restoration work through fiscal year 2033.
The interest stays set aside for wetlands programs instead of being added to the formula money states get for wildlife restoration, hunter education, and related uses.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Signed November 25, 2025; extends the requirement, which had been set to expire at the start of fiscal year 2026, through fiscal year 2033.
